# The Demo {#sec-the-demo}

| My third reply was not a sentence.
| In the last four, Hedda said,
| As always, "How's the book?" I asked
| "Can I show you?" instead.

| She looked at me a moment, then
| Turned her monitor my way.
| I had rehearsed it for a week:
| Each evening, I would stay

| At the kitchen table, run the tool
| On Full Stop, and talk through
| What it found, to nobody, against
| A four-minute timer, too.

| The first night took me nine. By the end
| Of the week, four would do,
| And I no longer needed notes,
| Which I brought anyway, too.

| It found the same thing every night;
| I liked it for that. There,
| The shop in four, the shop in nine,
| One claim they couldn't share.

| I knew where on the screen they'd sit,
| How long they'd take to land,
| And for the moment they appeared,
| I had a sentence at hand.

| I plugged into her monitor
| And ran it. It reads the list
| Of claims, then chapters; for each claim,
| Each sentence, none missed,

| With chapter, line. Most of them are green,
| And go too fast to read.
| The two shops, in under a second, came,
| Near the bottom, at speed:

| One claim; two sentences beneath,
| From chapters four and nine,
| On who had made the dash the fashion,
| Each with a different line.

| The claim was orange, as expected,
| Seven nights, every one.
| Beneath the shops were three more. Those
| I'd not expected: none.

| The night before, I'd fixed a thing.
| Chapter three held a date
| On the tool's list since the first Sunday,
| A decade off from eight.

| I'd made chapter three agree with eight.
| It took one sentence. Then
| I went to bed, pleased. I hadn't run
| The tool, after, again.

| I had rehearsed the demo; I
| Had not rehearsed the book.
| The date was not just in chapter three:
| It was in three more. Look:

| Three sentences, three chapters, which
| Had matched three's date for years,
| Untold. On Hedda's monitor
| The date, a claim, appears

| Once, at the top, and under it
| Five places where it stayed,
| Three in red, disagreeing with
| The sentence the night before I'd made.

| I'd had a sentence for the shops.
| For this, I'd nothing. So
| I showed her: pointed at the claim
| And each line under it, to show

| Which chapter it came from, and what about.
| It took more than the four.
| Easier than any answer, in three years,
| I'd given her before.

| I did not have to describe it: there,
| In five lines, on her screen.
| Hedda read it, not the summary
| At the bottom: what lay between.

| Around the third of the five lines,
| The half hour ran out.
| Hedda has a hard stop at the half hour.
| She watched all of it, throughout.

| She asked one question, in the middle.
| Pointing at the shops, she went
| Straight to the color, and asked me
| What the orange meant.

| "Contradicts, but I like it," I said.
| She wrote that down. And where,
| I don't know. When the tool was done,
| The screen held, sitting there,

| Four contradictions, and a count
| Below that told the score.
| Hedda sat back and looked a while,
| Then asked one question more:

| Was the book done? "No," I said.
| I heard myself say so.
| The true answer, for the first time,
| Was shorter than the show.

| She nodded, wrote something down, and we
| Both stood, nine minutes late.
| Her running document is shared with me;
| I open it more than I'll state.

| It changed again that week:
| *Book: demo.*
